issues.quote: He had been four years on that watch and he played it for anyone who would sit still.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the uncle's ownership of the repeater.
issues.misreading: A solver could take 'four years' as a timing or history clue about the watch and the uncle, which the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: It has given me trouble for ten years and I have never let anyone near it, my uncle included.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for how long Félix's watch has been troublesome.
issues.misreading: The 'ten years' figure is an unsupported duration hint about Félix's watch. It could be read as bearing on how far his watch is off, though the sheet does not say.

issues.quote: I remember because I thought, another ten minutes and I will be obliged to go down and drink to the century with everybody.
issues.fact: At the striking of ten, Félix's watch read 9:40 (twenty to ten). The sheet gives no sense of what he believed the real time to be.
issues.misreading: 'Another ten minutes' could be heard as a hint that he thought it was near 9:50 or that he had a sense of the true time, which the sheet does not support. It is a duration hint not in the fact sheet.
